foundation_surface_input_group.description: Rate per SF applies to net above-grade foundation wall area from PaintScope. Engine divides SF by rate to calculate hours.

task_production_rates.name: Landscape Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting along foundation perimeter where landscape is adjacent. ~30 sec per LF. Includes staking and securing tarps at grade line. LF-based. Identical rate to masonry wall sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Coverage adequate along working area. Minor gaps acceptable if no spray overspray risk.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full perimeter coverage of plantings within spray drift zone (10-15 ft). Secure against wind.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Walk Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay drop cloths and plastic on adjacent walkway surfaces at foundation base. ~14 sec per SF. Identical rate to masonry wall sibling.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Key areas covered. Minor gaps acceptable away from spray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of walkways within overspray zone.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Patio Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay drop cloths and plastic on adjacent patio surfaces at foundation base. ~14 sec per SF. Same process and rate as hardscape walk protection.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Key areas covered. Minor gaps acceptable away from spray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of patio within overspray zone.

task_production_rates.name: Moisture Content Testing
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Electronic moisture meter checks at multiple points across above-grade foundation band. MC >4% is HARD STOP (stricter than masonry wall 12% due to continuous ground contact). ~20 min fixed time for foundation scope — fewer test points than full masonry wall. 3-5 readings per elevation, document all readings.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Spot check representative areas. Surface reads <4% MC.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Multiple test points per elevation. All readings <4% MC. Documented.

task_production_rates.name: Form-Release Agent and Laitance Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove form-release agents and laitance from poured concrete foundation by wire brush, abrasive pad, or chemical detergent. ~24 sec per SF. Water bead test to verify removal. Poured concrete ONLY — not applicable to CMU. Same rate as masonry wall form-release task.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Form-release removed from coating areas. Water bead test passes on representative spots.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full removal. Water bead test passes on all areas. Surface absorbs water uniformly.

task_production_rates.name: Efflorescence Treatment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Stiff brush removal of efflorescence (white salt deposits), TSP wash if moderate. ~18 sec per SF. Must remove ALL efflorescence before coating — coating over active efflorescence causes osmotic blistering. Foundation is susceptible due to ground contact and capillary moisture rise. Conditional task — include_when efflorescence is present.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Loose efflorescence removed. No active white deposits on surface.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full removal. No visible efflorescence. Moisture source question addressed.

task_production_rates.name: Pressure Wash Foundation Surface

QT2.notes: Basic water wash to remove visible dirt and construction debris. Light pressure.

QT3.notes: Full water wash with stiff brush. TSP solution for stubborn areas. Rinse thoroughly.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Low-pressure water wash for new concrete/CMU foundation surface. Research range 500-800 SF/hr. Foundation is ground-level and accessible — faster than masonry wall (no elevation repositioning). QT2 basic rinse, QT3 thorough wash with TSP. 24 hr dry time before coating (not included in rate).

defect_tolerance.QT2: Visible dirt and debris removed. Surface appears clean.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All construction dust, dirt, and debris removed. TSP scrub on stains. Allow 24 hr dry time.

task_production_rates.name: Foundation Crack Patching
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Patch hairline and minor cracks in foundation wall with hydraulic cement or masonry patching compound. ~48 sec per LF. Cracks wider than 1/4 inch are structural — flag for GC. Foundation cracks are common in new construction from curing shrinkage.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Visible cracks filled. Patch flush with surface.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All cracks patched. Patches smooth and flush. No voids in patch material.

task_production_rates.name: Bug Hole Patching (Poured Concrete)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fill surface voids (bug holes) in poured concrete with hydraulic cement. ~2 min per hole. Bug holes are air voids from concrete placement — cosmetic defect on formed surfaces. Poured concrete only. Trowel smooth, flush with surface.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Large bug holes filled. Small holes (<1/8 inch) may remain.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All visible bug holes filled. Patches smooth and flush with surface.

task_production_rates.name: Surface Profile Preparation
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Achieve CSP 1-2 (smooth to light profile) for thin cosmetic coating. Diamond grind or acid etch on smooth poured concrete to open pores for primer adhesion. ~12 sec per SF. Foundation is ground-level — easy access with floor grinder or hand tools. Conditional — only needed when surface is too smooth for primer adhesion.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Surface accepts primer. Water absorption test passes.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform surface profile. Water absorbs evenly across all areas.

task_production_rates.name: Block Filler - Spray Application (CMU)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray application of block filler on CMU foundation. Foundation is ground-level with easy sprayer access — faster than masonry wall block filler (150 SF/hr 2-person crew with backroll). Foundation spray does NOT require backroll per research (above-grade cosmetic coating). 400 SF/hr single operator. Heavy-body material through 531 tip, 30-mesh filter. Single coat. CMU only.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Voids filled to PCA P12 Level 2 standard. No unfilled voids visible.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All voids filled. Verify complete void coverage. PCA P12 Level 2 achieved.

task_production_rates.name: Block Filler - Heavy Roller Application (CMU)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Heavy roller (1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap) application of block filler on CMU foundation. ~30 sec per SF. Multiple passes to force thick filler into voids. Foundation is ground-level — slightly faster than elevated masonry wall (80 SF/hr). Single coat. CMU only.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Voids filled. Multiple passes if needed.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All voids filled. Heavy pressure. PCA P12 Level 2 verified.

task_production_rates.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer - Spray Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray (517 tip, 60-mesh filter) of alkali-resistant primer on foundation. ~6 sec per SF. Ground-level access, continuous runs along foundation band — fast spray production. Spray-only valid on smooth poured concrete (no backroll needed per research). CMU foundation with spray SHOULD include backroll per masonry doctrine — but that is a separate spray_backroll method, not this task. Single coat. Mandatory on ALL new foundation (pH 12-14).

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays or thin spots.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform mil build. Full surface saturation. No dry spots.

task_production_rates.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer - Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roller (3/4 inch nap poured, 1-1/4 inch nap CMU) application of alkali-resistant primer. ~18 sec per SF. Ground-level, easy access with extension pole on short foundation band. Faster than masonry wall primer roll (125 SF/hr) because foundation is accessible at grade and band is short. Single coat.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. Primer worked into all pores. Maintain wet edge.

task_production_rates.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer - Brush Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush application of primer on foundation. Detail work around pipes, vents, and tight areas only. ~55 sec per SF. Must work primer into surface texture. Same rate as masonry wall brush primer — brush pace is substrate-limited regardless of access.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. Primer worked into surface.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage. All surface texture saturated.

task_production_rates.name: Acrylic Finish - Spray Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray of acrylic masonry finish on primed foundation. ~5.5 sec per SF. Ground-level continuous run along foundation band — excellent spray production. Spray-only valid on smooth poured concrete per research (no backroll needed for cosmetic coating on non-porous primed surface). Per-coat rate. QT2 = 1 coat, QT3 = 2 coats.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays. Single coat.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform mil build. Consistent appearance. No dry spots.

task_production_rates.name: Acrylic Finish - Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roller application of acrylic finish on primed foundation. ~18 sec per SF. 3/4 inch nap for poured concrete, 1-1/4 inch nap for CMU. Ground-level, easy access. Faster than masonry wall finish roll (150 SF/hr) due to ground-level access and simpler surface geometry. Per-coat rate.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Consistent roller texture. Maintain wet edge. Uniform appearance.

task_production_rates.name: Cementitious Coating (Drylok-type) - Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roller application of cementitious/crystalline coating (Drylok-type) on primed foundation. ~26 sec per SF. Heavier body material than acrylic — thicker application, lower coverage rate. 3/4 inch nap for poured concrete, 1-1/4 inch nap for CMU. Ground-level access. Per-coat rate.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. Material worked into surface.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. No thin spots. Full surface sealed.

task_production_rates.name: Cementitious Coating (Drylok-type) - Brush Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush application of cementitious coating on foundation. ~48 sec per SF. Detail work and small areas. Heavier material requires more effort to brush out evenly. Per-coat rate.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. Material worked into surface texture.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage. Uniform appearance. No thin spots.

task_production_rates.name: Detail Brush Work (Pipes, Vents, Transitions)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Detail brush work around foundation penetrations (pipes, vents, conduit) and at siding-to-foundation transition. ~55 sec per SF. Careful work to maintain clean lines at grade-line gap (MASK the gap — NEVER caulk). Rate is per SF of detail area, not total foundation wall. Per-coat rate.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Penetrations coated. Reasonable coverage.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All penetrations fully coated. Clean transition at siding interface. Grade-line gap properly masked.

task_production_rates.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Ground-level walkthrough of all foundation elevations. Check for holidays, missed spots, coating uniformity. Foundation is a small scope — 15-20 min covers full perimeter. Verify grade-line gap is still clear (not accidentally sealed). Check protection zones for overspray.

defect_tolerance.QT2: No obvious misses visible from standing distance.
defect_tolerance.QT3: No defects visible at 3-6 ft. Coating uniform. Grade-line gap clear.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. ~48 sec per SF of touched-up area. Rate is per SF of area needing touch-up, not total foundation. Foundation typically needs minimal touch-up — simple surface geometry. Ground-level access.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Obvious misses touched up.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All noted defects repaired. Touch-ups blended.

task_production_rates.name: Protection Material Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all landscape tarps, hardscape covers, tape, and plastic sheeting. ~20 min for foundation scope (smaller than masonry wall). Check for tape adhesive residue. Verify no paint on protected surfaces. Small scope — quick teardown.

defect_tolerance.QT2: All protection materials removed.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All materials removed. No tape residue. Check landscape for overspray.

task_production_rates.name: Tool and Equipment Cleaning
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clean brushes, rollers, trays, sprayer (if used). Foundation is small scope — less equipment to clean than masonry wall. ~18 min. Dispose of saturated roller covers. If sprayer used: flush cycle takes longer (~25 min total — use 18 min as average across spray and roll methods).

defect_tolerance.QT2: Equipment cleaned and stored.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full clean. Equipment ready for next use. Roller covers disposed.

factor_modifiers.name: Foundation Substrate Type Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Foundation type affects production rate due to porosity and surface characteristics. Poured concrete is baseline (smooth, dense, low absorption). CMU is slower due to porous surface, voids, and surface irregularity.
factor_modifiers.notes: Poured concrete is baseline (smooth formed surface, dense, consistent absorption). CMU is 15% slower due to porous block surface, irregular geometry, and mortar joints between blocks. Maximum 1.15x modifier. Foundation_type is the ONLY modifier for this spec — no access, coating system, or environmental modifiers. Well under 4.0x stacking cap.

quality_effects.notes: Economy tier. Single finish coat on primed surface. No interstage work. Block filler still required on CMU (structural, not quality-optional). Most common tier for utilitarian foundation band.

Standard tier. Two finish coats. No interstage sanding or inspection (utilitarian surface does not warrant interstage cycle even at QT3). Clean transition at grade line. Higher-end residential where foundation appearance matters.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Poured concrete, acrylic, ground access, QT3 baseline (roll)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Best case — smooth poured concrete at ground level. 200 SF/hr single operator.
CMU at ground level. 174 SF/hr. Slightly slower due to porous block surface.
Slowest finish combination — cementitious on CMU. 122 SF/hr. Still ground-level. Heavier material on porous substrate.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Poured concrete, acrylic, ground access, QT3 (spray)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Fastest finish production — spray acrylic on smooth poured concrete. 650 SF/hr single operator. Typical for long continuous foundation runs.

assumptions.value: Ground-level access for all tasks. No height modifier.
assumptions.source: Research KD-008. Foundation band is at grade by definition.
assumptions.note: FAC_EXT_ACCESS is NOT applicable. Sloped lots exposing extra foundation height are an edge case not modeled.

assumptions.source: Research RC-002. Established exterior spec convention.
assumptions.note: Wind, sun exposure, surface temperature are SOP concerns, not estimatable at bid time. Foundation at ground level has less wind impact than elevated work.

assumptions.value: Spray on poured concrete foundation does NOT require backroll.
assumptions.source: Research CD-005 notes. Above-grade cosmetic coating on smooth poured concrete does not require forced pore penetration.
assumptions.note: CMU foundation with spray SHOULD include backroll per masonry doctrine — this is handled by method selection (user would choose roll or spray+detail brush for CMU rather than spray-only).

assumptions.value: Protection teardown as FIXED time (20 min) rather than LF-based.
assumptions.source: Engineering judgment. Foundation is small scope — total protection material is limited.
assumptions.note: Masonry wall uses LF-based teardown (200 LF/hr) for larger scope. Foundation is small enough that fixed time is more appropriate and simpler.

risks.description: Block filler spray rate (400 SF/hr) assumes ground-level single operator without backroll. If CMU foundation requires spray+backroll (per masonry doctrine), rate should drop to ~200 SF/hr with 2-person crew.
risks.mitigation: Research indicates spray-only is acceptable for above-grade cosmetic foundation coating. Monitor field feedback. If backroll is needed, add TSK_FNDN_BLOCK_FILL_SPRAY_BACKROLL variant at 200 SF/hr.

risks.description: Cementitious coating (Drylok-type) production rates are estimated from acrylic roll rates with a reduction for heavier material. No direct field calibration data for cementitious on foundation.
risks.mitigation: Rates align with manufacturer application guides (100-175 SF/hr roll). Flag for field calibration on first cementitious foundation project.

risks.description: Fixed-time tasks (moisture test, inspect, teardown, tool clean) assume standard foundation scope (200 LF perimeter, 24-inch band). Larger foundations (e.g., walkout basements with 6+ ft exposure) may need more time.
risks.mitigation: Engine allows rate adjustment per task. Field estimator can increase fixed times for larger foundation scopes. Document in SOP notes.

validation_plan.description: Time a standard foundation coating project (200 LF perimeter, 24-inch band, ~400 SF) from setup to cleanup.
validation_plan.expected_range: 4-8 hours total (QT3, roll, poured concrete, acrylic, 2 finish coats).
validation_plan.calibrates: All task rates and overall project duration.

validation_plan.description: Compare poured concrete vs CMU foundation production rates on matched-size projects.
validation_plan.expected_range: CMU should be 10-20% slower than poured concrete across prep, prime, and finish tasks.

validation_plan.description: Time cementitious (Drylok) roll application vs acrylic roll application on matched surfaces.
validation_plan.expected_range: Cementitious should be 25-40% slower than acrylic due to heavier body material.

validation_plan.description: Time block filler application on CMU foundation (both spray and roll methods).
